Go to batchTasted
  1. 1 JulVersion 1 · 50 g oil · 800 gchurned 2 Aug · Latest
  2. 4 OctVersion 2draft

What the sheet is served under. Prints as the title. Copies into the next version.

Ingredients

Ingredient% of batch
Step 2Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
gWhole milkestimated 120 g of 370.4 g · 46.3% in all15.0%
gSucrose 12 g of 76.0 g · 9.5% in all1.5%
gLocust bean gum 0.1%
gGuar gum 0.1%
gLambda carrageenan trace
Step 3Build the base
gWhole milkestimated250.4 g of 370.4 g · 46.3% in all31.3%
gHeavy creamestimated 31.6%
gSkim milk powder 2.8%
gSucrose64 g of 76.0 g · 9.5% in all8.0%
gDextrose 1.5%
gFine sea saltestimated 0.4%
Step 6Allulose in, then crash-cool
gAlluloseestimated 2.5%
Step 8Emulsify the oil, cold
gGraza Drizzle 5.0%
gSoy lecithin 0.2%
799.7 gTotal

Instructions

Before you start

  1. 1

    Lecithin into the oil. Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.

    temproom

    It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

    ·

  2. 2

    Gum slurry — the only high-heat step. Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.

    temp85 °Chold2 min

    At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

    ·

  3. 3

    Build the base. Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.

    blend60 s

    ·

  4. 4

    Divide. Tare, pour, check.

    per jar379 g

    Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.

    Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

    ·

  5. 5

    Pasteurise in the circulator. Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.

    temp69 °Chold40 mincome-up10–12 min

    With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.

    Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

    ·

  6. 6

    Allulose in, then crash-cool. Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.

    tobelow 5 °C

    Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

    ·

  7. 7

    Age. Hold covered in the fridge.

    temp4 °Ctime12–24 h

    ·

  8. 8

    Emulsify the oil, cold. Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.

    temp4 °Cblend45 s

    Never heat this oil.

    ·

  9. 9

    Churn. Freeze immediately.

    overrun25–30%

    ·

  10. 10

    Harden, and serve warm. Harden, then temper before serving.

    harden−20 °C, 4+ hserve−11 to −12 °C

    ·

Milkfat 13.0% and added fat 5.0% — 28% of fat.

Computed from coefficient set 2026.1 (slice transcription). PAC relative to sucrose = 100, the same reference basis lactose's own PAC (100) is expressed against; lactose is taken as 54.5% of MSNF. Whole milk, Heavy cream, Allulose, and Fine sea salt are estimated.

Guar gum at 0.48 g and Lambda carrageenan at 0.16 g are under the Kitchen scale's resolution. The master blend for 4 batches ahead: Locust bean gum 4.16 g, Guar gum 1.92 g, Lambda carrageenan 0.64 g, 6.72 g in all, with 1.68 g taken for this batch. basis: Kitchen scale reads to 1 g; the equipment profile blends 4 batches ahead.

Whole milk at 370.4 g and Heavy cream at 252.8 g carry an ultra-pasteurised heat treatment: 623.2 g of the batch's 799.7 g. basis: heat treatment recorded on each ingredient.

Locust bean gum hydrates at 82 °C, above the 69 °C pasteurisation hold. Step 2 targets 85 °C. basis: the ingredient's recorded hydration temperature and the version's pasteurisation setting; the step's typed target.

                  Olive Oil Ice Cream, circulator

                  Scaled 0.8× from the 1 kg formula. All ratios unchanged — PAC, POD, fat, MSNF and total solids are identical to the full batch. Sized to two 16 oz Ball jars in a circulator bath.

                  Next version · draft from Version 1
                  From batch

                  Go to batchTasted
                  1. 1 JulVersion 1 · 50 g oil · 800 gchurned 2 Aug · Latest
                  2. 4 OctVersion 2draft

                  What the sheet is served under. Prints as the title. Copies into the next version.

                  Ingredients

                  Ingredient% of batch
                  Step 2Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
                  gWhole milkestimated 120 g of 370.4 g · 46.3% in all15.0%
                  gSucrose 12 g of 76.0 g · 9.5% in all1.5%
                  gLocust bean gum 0.1%
                  gGuar gum 0.1%
                  gLambda carrageenan trace
                  Step 3Build the base
                  gWhole milkestimated250.4 g of 370.4 g · 46.3% in all31.3%
                  gHeavy creamestimated 31.6%
                  gSkim milk powder 2.8%
                  gSucrose64 g of 76.0 g · 9.5% in all8.0%
                  gDextrose 1.5%
                  gFine sea saltestimated 0.4%
                  Step 6Allulose in, then crash-cool
                  gAlluloseestimated 2.5%
                  Step 8Emulsify the oil, cold
                  gGraza Drizzle 5.0%
                  gSoy lecithin 0.2%
                  799.7 gTotal

                  Before you start

                  • from 50 g oil · 800 g

                  Instructions

                  1. 1

                    Lecithin into the oil. Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.

                    temproom

                    It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

                    ·

                  2. 2

                    Gum slurry — the only high-heat step. Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.

                    temp85 °Chold2 min

                    At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

                    ·

                  3. 3

                    Build the base. Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.

                    blend60 s

                    ·

                  4. 4

                    Divide. Tare, pour, check.

                    per jar379 g

                    Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.

                    Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

                    ·

                  5. 5

                    Pasteurise in the circulator. Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.

                    temp69 °Chold40 mincome-up10–12 min

                    With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.

                    Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

                    ·

                  6. 6

                    Allulose in, then crash-cool. Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.

                    tobelow 5 °C

                    Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

                    ·

                  7. 7

                    Age. Hold covered in the fridge.

                    temp4 °Ctime12–24 h

                    ·

                  8. 8

                    Emulsify the oil, cold. Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.

                    temp4 °Cblend45 s

                    Never heat this oil.

                    ·

                  9. 9

                    Churn. Freeze immediately.

                    overrun25–30%

                    ·

                  10. 10

                    Harden, and serve warm. Harden, then temper before serving.

                    harden−20 °C, 4+ hserve−11 to −12 °C

                    ·

                  Milkfat 13.0% and added fat 5.0% — 28% of fat.

                  Computed from coefficient set 2026.1 (slice transcription). PAC relative to sucrose = 100, the same reference basis lactose's own PAC (100) is expressed against; lactose is taken as 54.5% of MSNF. Whole milk, Heavy cream, Allulose, and Fine sea salt are estimated.

                  Guar gum at 0.48 g and Lambda carrageenan at 0.16 g are under the Kitchen scale's resolution. The master blend for 4 batches ahead: Locust bean gum 4.16 g, Guar gum 1.92 g, Lambda carrageenan 0.64 g, 6.72 g in all, with 1.68 g taken for this batch. basis: Kitchen scale reads to 1 g; the equipment profile blends 4 batches ahead.

                  Whole milk at 370.4 g and Heavy cream at 252.8 g carry an ultra-pasteurised heat treatment: 623.2 g of the batch's 799.7 g. basis: heat treatment recorded on each ingredient.

                  Locust bean gum hydrates at 82 °C, above the 69 °C pasteurisation hold. Step 2 targets 85 °C. basis: the ingredient's recorded hydration temperature and the version's pasteurisation setting; the step's typed target.

                  Freezing · PAC through Whole milk, Heavy cream, Allulose, Fine sea salt; Sweetness · POD through Whole milk, Heavy cream, Allulose; Milk solids · MSNF through Whole milk, Heavy cream; Solids through Whole milk, Heavy cream. basis: the per-field basis recorded on each ingredient.
